plan: Since my private value is $3, the rational strategy is to bid slightly below this value to avoid overpaying. Bidding my exact value or higher risks a loss if I win, as I would pay more than the item's worth to me. A bid of $2.9 maximizes potential profit while minimizing risk, as it allows me to win only if other bids are lower, ensuring I pay less than my value.

Given that my value for the prize is $24, I should bid slightly below this value to maximize profit if I win while minimizing the risk of overpaying. Rational bidders will bid below their values to avoid negative profit. A reasonable bid is slightly less than my value, say $23. This balances the risk of overbidding and the chance of winning.

My value is $11. To maximize profit, bid slightly below my value, considering the risk of overbidding relative to others. Rational bidders won't bid more than their value. Bidding $10.9 ensures a small profit if others bid below my value. Bidding above $11 risks loss if the second-highest bid is higher.
